original_card.question: Can one measured replay bottleneck be sped up without dropping coverage?
methods: Profile one isolated replay and optimize the measured bottleneck.
Design source-bound reuse with explicit dependency invalidation and negative controls.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Report before/after wall time on the same fixture, retained checks and invalidation behavior.

first_step.inspect: Resolve the current selected review, separate complex/ordinary BIT/admitted BIT/outer budgets, and compare the card against live handoffs before starting. Historical ceilings require exact source/model equivalence.
first_step.scope: Source-binding orientation only; not a scientific replay or all-size proof. Materialize selected inputs if this checkout is sparse.

original_card.first_experiment: Measure one unchanged fixture, preserve check coverage, and test one optimization with invalidation controls.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Faster trustworthy replays increase review throughput and let mechanism candidates be checked sooner.
allowed_variations: Profile one stage or design one source-bound cache boundary.
scope_change_triggers: Skipping coverage or comparing different fixtures to claim speedup.

actual_scope: Package the P104 designer toolkit (exact pricing and legality oracle, verifier-profile adoption, the #6030 rebuild pipeline with the fold/hoist/retain constructor passes, the gen2/gen3 generators, sub-circuit extract/splice/re-solve tools, bulk evaluation and the floor LPs) as one reviewable tool with a regression suite. No word and no kappa claim.
scope_change_reason: The replay-runtime card asks for a measured replay speed-up; this package ships the tooling and its exact-replay regression suite, including the rebuild chain and native replay kernels that were sped up while it was built, but makes no new performance claim. Recorded as changed.
bottleneck_link: Side result (tooling). Comparing and extending frontier words requires the same exact invoice, localised legality verdict and constructor passes to be recomputed on any P104-family word; this makes the #6030 -> #6144 -> #6167 constructor steps reproducible by one command.
stop_rule: Keep the package only if tests/regress.py --fast reproduces every exact number it wraps (kappa of the PR5545/5551/5553/5561/5907/5827 words, localised mutants, native replay equality) and the rebuild smoke reproduces #6030 at exact kappa; otherwise report the failing check instead of shipping.
evidence: VERIFY.json runs tests/regress.py --fast (exact prices of six published words, localised legality mutants, native replay equality, screens executed on #5660, shipcheck, surgery round trip, rebuild mini chain at exact kappa .003125811557911897) and the retain pass on #6144 -> #6167.
author: DreamingOfClouds, with Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), via Claude Code
ai_assistance: Prepared with Claude Opus 5.5 via Claude Code: Claude wrote and edited the tooling and tests under DreamingOfClouds' direction. Every command reproduces numbers published by the PRs it wraps or by exact recomputation; no independent human or proof-kernel acceptance is claimed.

open_questions.question: Can the unshipped model inputs of planbuild (plan search population and class-break picks) be packaged so plan.py/build.py run from a fresh clone?
open_questions.why_it_matters: planbuild is shipped as source only; its published totals are not replayed in CI.
open_questions.first_step: List the modules plan.py and build.py import and vendor the minimal closure.

open_questions.question: Can the fold pass (about 15 minutes per site) be made fast enough for generic CI to replay #6030 -> #6144 end to end?
open_questions.why_it_matters: CI currently replays the retain pass and the rebuild smoke only.
open_questions.blocked_by: Runtime of the exact IOROOT-style solve per site.
open_questions.first_step: Profile alignbuild/iob2.py on one site and cache the rule matrices.
